stem: In a college, 60% of students come from city schools and 40% come from rural schools. In an aptitude test, 30% of city-school students and 50% of rural-school students score above 80 marks. A student who scored above 80 marks is selected at random. What is the probability that this student is from a city school?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Returning the prior P(City) = 0.6 = 3/5, ignoring the test score information and failing to apply Bayes theorem.
Computing P(Rural|>80) = 0.20/0.38 = 10/19, returning the posterior for rural students instead of city students.
Correctly computing 18/38 but failing to simplify the fraction to 9/19, leaving the answer in unreduced form.

explanation_sections.punchline: A high score is actually more likely from a rural student here, so the city posterior (9/19) is below the city prior (3/5).
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: Bayes theorem with two hypotheses. Compute joint probabilities: City and >80 = 0.18; Rural and >80 = 0.20. Total = 0.38. P(City|>80) = 0.18/0.38 = 9/19.
explanation_sections.lesson: After observing an outcome, if one group has a higher rate of that outcome, its posterior rises relative to its prior.
explanation_sections.timing: 80 seconds. Multiply both branches, add for denominator, divide. The trap is using the prior 3/5 without updating.
